messages:
elaine-support: heads up — APAC customers (JP/AU/SG) are reporting huge request latencies and some 401 spikes since ~09:10 UTC. Multiple escalations from support inbox.

sre_ian: on it. seeing a jump in p50/p95 for ap-southeast-1. pulling routing decision logs now.

elaine-support: one example from customer: curl to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate returns 200 but latency 1.2s and they see token errors intermittently. I have request-id 0b8f2a.

devon: can you paste the request headers & the routing decision for that id?

elaine-support: pasted:

```
> GET /v1/generate
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx
> X-Client-Region: ap-southeast-1
> Request-Id: 0b8f2a
```

routing log (trimmed):
```
[09:11:02Z] request_id=0b8f2a src_region=ap-southeast-1 route_policy=latency check_capacity=ap-southeast-1 result=FALLBACK fallback_region=eu-west-1 reason="no available capacity" cache_used=true
[09:11:02Z] decision: assign -> eu-west-1
[09:11:03Z] auth_proxy: token_lookup=ok region_hint=eu-west-1
```

ashok: that cache_used=true line worries me — might be a cached fallback decision stored at the edge. if a cached negative decision pointed to eu-west, subsequent APAC traffic could be getting misrouted even after capacity returned.

sre_ian: yep i see repeated lines: fallback decision cached in routing-edge for 300s. Capacity in ap-southeast was fluctuating 09:05-09:12 and then recovered at 09:14 but cache TTL still active.

maria-sales: customers are seeing billing spikes for eu-hosted tokens (higher egress) — complaining about unexpected cross-region costs. we have 5 open tickets.

devon: also seeing a small uptick in 401s where auth service reported token region mismatch: auth-service validated token against eu keyring because request was routed to eu, but client's session expected ap keys -> intermittent 401.

elaine-support: repro steps for support engineers:
1) curl with X-Client-Region: ap-southeast-1 and record Request-Id header
2) check routing logs with that id in k8s-logs/routing-edge
3) if routing shows fallback_region != src_region, check cache TTL and edge node id

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-8425 — auto-notify sent to SRE and Routing teams.

sre_ian: immediate mitigation applied at 09:21 UTC: flushed routing-edge fallback caches globally and reduced fallback cache TTL from 300s -> 30s while we validate. Also added a temporary rule to prefer local region when capacity reported >= 60%.

ashok: rolled fix confirmed at 09:22 — APAC p95 dropped from ~1.3s to 120ms for the test customer.

sam-pm: what caused the initial misrouting to be cached? was it a code rollback or transient capacity report?

devon: root trigger appears to be a probe-side effect: a monitoring job saturated one APAC edge zone at 09:03 which led autoscaler to mark nodegroup out-of-capacity -> routing fallback wrote a negative decision into the edge cache. Two things compounded it: (1) the cache TTL was long (5m) and (2) cache keys didn't include a short-lived capacity token so subsequent requests used stale fallback policy.

maria-sales: timeline for customers: when did cross-region billing start? we need to notify finance & affected customers.

sre_ian: cross-region routing started ~09:10 and peaked ~09:12. We throttled it back at 09:21 by flushing caches. Recommend notifying customers in the 09:10-09:21 window; ops will send billing note.

elaine-support: support message draft to customers (ready to send after PM review):

"We investigated increased latencies and unexpected billing during 09:10-09:21 UTC. A cached routing fallback caused some APAC requests to route to EU. We have flushed the cache and implemented a temporary TTL reduction. We're investigating follow-ups and will share a postmortem. Apologies for the disruption and any unexpected charges." :handshake:

sam-pm: please don't send billing wording until finance confirms credits. I'll loop in finance.

devon: quick config snippet that was the culprit (edge config):
```
fallback_cache: enabled
fallback_cache_ttl_seconds: 300  # old
# missing: include_capacity_token_in_key: true
```

ashok: action items I propose now:
- short-term: keep cache TTL=30s for 24h, add preflight flush on abnormal autoscaler events (done)
- med-term: change cache key to include recent capacity token + region stamp (devon)
- long-term: add circuit-breaker so fallback decisions don't apply to >X% of global requests (sre_ian + infra)

devon: i will open PR to change key + tests (link: https://git.redwood.internal/changes/PR-3345). ETA EOD today for tests, Wed for rollout behind a feature flag.

maria-sales: +1 for customer comms once finance gives guidance. we need a clear list of affected orgs for credits. support will aggregate tickets.

elaine-support: final note: several support threads reported 401s — after cache flush 401 rate dropped but we should run a session token audit to confirm no lingering auth issues.

sre_ian: confirming post-incident: root cause = stale fallback routing cached at edge caused by transient autoscaler capacity signal + long TTL. Contributing: cache key did not include capacity token. Impact: ~09:10-09:21 UTC — increased latencies for APAC customers, cross-region token/auth anomalies, billing footprint shift to EU for affected requests. Mitigation: global cache flush, TTL reduction, temporary routing preference change. Next steps: implement cache-key fix, circuit-breaker, add monitoring alert for unusual fallback cache churn.

sam-pm: CC'ing compliance & finance. we will draft a short postmortem doc and schedule 1hr follow-up retro tomorrow.

elaine-support: thanks all. closing thread after postmortem doc.
